@@41456294 <p> http : **31;133;TOOLONG for NodeSat , 28 Dec 2019 16:01:02 GMTSuccess gets the space program back on track after a previous attempt in July 2017 failed mid-launch &gt;https : **33;166;TOOLONG ... Friday launched one of the world&amp;#8217 ; s most powerful rockets in a major step forward for its planned mission to Mars in 2020. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The heavy lift Long March 5 rocket carrying a Shijian 20 test satellite payload blasted off from the Wenchang launch site on the southern island of Hainan at 8:45 pm ( 1245 GMT ) , a livestream from state broadcaster CCTV showed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;&amp;#8220 ; After more than 2,000 seconds , the Shijian 20 satellite was sent into its predetermined orbit , &amp;#8221 ; the official Xinhua news agency reported . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The rocket launch &amp;#8220 ; tests key technologies related to future space missions , &amp;#8221 ; Xinhua said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The successful launch is a key part of China&amp;#8217 ; s ambitious plans for a mission to the Red Planet next year and hopes of having a crewed space station by 2022. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;&amp;#8220 ; The Long March 5 rocket is tasked with important missions , &amp;#8221 ; Wu Yanhua , the deputy head of China&amp;#8217 ; s National Space Administration , said in a video released by CCTV last week . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;&amp;#8220 ; It will be tasked with a series of key missions including launching China&amp;#8217 ; s first Mars probe , the Chang&amp;#8217 ; e-5 lunar probe and a core module for the manned space station . &amp;#8221 ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;More than a million people watched an online livestream of the launch and crowds gathered near the island launch site cheered as the rocket blasted off into the night sky , videos posted on social media showed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;&amp;#8220 ; Fat Five , &amp;#8221 ; the rocket&amp;#8217 ; s nickname , was a trending topic on the Twitter-like Weibo social media platform . &lt;/p&gt; **25;201;TOOLONG ; s success gets the space program back on track after a previous attempt in July 2017 failed mid-launch. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The Long March 5 Y2 was supposed to put the Shijian 18 experimental communications satellite into orbit and its failure delayed plans to use the rocket in a planned mission to collect lunar samples in the second half of 2017. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;China successfully launched the first Long March 5 in November 2016 , which it said at the time was the most powerful launcher it had yet developed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The Long March 5 , which is capable of carrying up to 25 tons , is comparable in capacity to the US-made Delta IV Heavy and Russia&amp;#8217 ; s Proton-M , some of the most powerful launchers in existence , according to NASASpaceFlight.com. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;By contrast the US&amp;#8217 ; s Saturn V , which delivered astronauts to the Moon in 1969 , was designed to deliver some 140 tonnes of payload into low Earth orbit . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h4&gt;Space ambitions&lt;/h4&gt; &lt;p&gt;Beijing has invested billions of dollars in its space program in an effort to catch up with its rival the United States and affirm its status as a major world power . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;In 2003 , the Asian giant , which now spends more than Russia and Japan on its civil and military space programs , became only the third nation to put a human into orbit . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;In January 2019 , China became the first nation to land a probe on the far side of the Moon . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The Chang&amp;#8217 ; e-4 lander -- named after the Moon goddess in Chinese mythology -- released a rover in the Moon&amp;#8217 ; s South Pole-Aitken Basin shortly after New Year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;In November China completed a test of its Mars exploration lander , ahead of its first mission to the Red Planet slated for 2020 which is planned to deploy a rover to explore the Martian surface . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;China also aims to have a manned space station in orbit in 2022. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The Tiangong -- or &amp;#8220 ; Heavenly Palace&amp;#8221 ; -- is set to replace the International Space Station , which is due to be retired in 2024. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;China will also seek to build an international lunar base , possibly using 3D printing technology , in the future , Wu said in January . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;China&amp;#8217 ; s space program has alarmed the US , which fears that Beijing will threaten its dominance in space . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The White House announced the creation of a new military arm called the Space Force earlier this month , with President Donald Trump calling space &amp;#8220 ; the world&amp;#8217 ; s newest warfighting domain . &amp;#8221 ; Wilcox might have added that Japan was also a vital resource for the Soviet Union who took control over Korea down to the 38th parallel in 1945. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The Russians knew exactly what they were looking for , and they got it . Korea , until the end of the war annexed by Japan since 1910 ( a deal blessed by President Theodore Roosevelt ) was the most important part of Japan&amp;#8217 ; s atomic bomb program . The allies , especially the United States , did not know that . The Russians did . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;While it can&amp;#8217 ; t be proven today , I believe that the Russian spy in Tokyo , &lt;a href= " https : **33;290;TOOLONG ... Sorge&lt;/a&gt; , hanged by the Japanese in November 1944 , provided vital information on Japan&amp;#8217 ; s atomic bomb program to his NKVD bosses . No doubt it was his information that gave Lavrentiy Beria , the NKVD head , the scientific information he needed to pursue the bomb , and Stalin put him in charge of the project ( showing clearly that the Soviets depended on the flow of intelligence for their A-bomb effort ) . Stalin also took advantage of Truman&amp;#8217 ; s invitation to intervene in Mongolia and Korea almost at the end of the war . As Wilcox points out , the toughest fighting was when the Russians took control of the Konan ( Hungnam ) area where Japan&amp;#8217 ; s nuclear work was centered in Korea . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Japan had ( at least ) two major atomic bomb programs , one run by the Japanese army and headed by Yoshio Nishina of Japan&amp;#8217 ; s Institute of Physical and Chemical Research ( RIKEN ) and the other run by Bonsaku Arakatsu who ran the navy&amp;#8217 ; s F-Go atomic bomb project . Both men were top physicists , and Nishina had strong connections to Albert Einstein , Ernest Lawrence at the University of California and Niels Bohr ( whom Nishina again visited after the end of World War II ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;It was the navy project that used Korea for uranium enrichment and thorium processing . On a total returns basis , Asian credit has returned 11-12% depending on the bond 's risk profile . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; " Most of the performance is coming from rates -- for example , the 100 basis point rally would alone give a 5-year bond a 4%+ return . Also , there has been a squeeze in credit spreads , " said Rogerio Bernardo , Head of global syndicate , DBS referring to the decline in the US Treasury yields , a benchmark for credit valuation . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The 10-year US government bond had dropped 122 basis points this year at its lowest in September . In recent months , Beijing has been restraining inflow of excess liquidity into property developers ' hands to put a cap on land acquisition costs , which would raise property prices . But authorities are unlikely to choke funds availability because overall stability in the property sector is still of paramount importance to the world 's second-largest economy . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; " The authorities have managed the demand and supply side of the property market well in 2019 , as evidenced by stability in residential prices . Significant changes in policy direction or excessive tightening are hence unlikely , in our view , " said a UBS CIO note . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; " Some liquidity will eventually flow back into the property sector despite negative headline news on governments ' efforts to control prices . " &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;HSBC is also overweight on China property after changing its recommendation from neutral this month . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; " We expect the government to gradually loosen its policy on home purchase restrictions and/or price caps , and also believe that better onshore liquidity will improve market access for developers , " it said in a report . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Credit Suisse analysts say the Chinese property is a preferred sector , with revenue and earnings expected to grow by 21% and 18% in 2020 , respectively . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; " We expect authorities to support real estate investment growth in 2020 . We expect more in 1H 2020 , " it said in a report . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The optimism has been sparked by the latest round of government measures to promote social mobility by reforming the hukou system . &lt;p&gt;Since his October swearing-in , Makarim also called for a broad program of deregulation , an end to year-end National Examinations &amp;#8212 ; regarded as worthless by many educators -- and a sweeping redesign of the education system to conform better with what is required in the modern workplace . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;But 2020 is already shaping up to be a make-or-break year for the 35-year-old founder of the US$10 billion Gojek ride-hailing and services platform , the youngest minister to have ever held the education portfolio . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The shakeup in the education system is part of President Joko Widodo 's new emphasis on human development , which he said in his state of the nation address last August is key to competing in the international marketplace . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Makarim 's approach fits with the need to build up a more highly skilled workforce that meets the expectations of the private sector and allows Indonesia to escape from its developing economy status . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;According to Statistics Indonesia , more than 40% of working age Indonesians have only a primary school education , while just 9% of the labor force has a university degree , often achieved without any serious test in critical thinking . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The biggest challenge to Makarim 's Merdeka Belanjar ( Freedom to Learn ) program ? : An entrenched bureaucracy stubbornly opposed to reform for ideological , material and even cultural reasons . &lt;/p&gt; " He 's a good administrator , but it takes a very good politician to win a fight against the bureaucracy like that in education . " &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The son of a prominent Jakarta lawyer whose family , by one close relative 's admission , has always been " obsessed with education , " Makarim received only his early education in Indonesia . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;He later enrolled in a Singapore boarding school before heading to the Ivy League in the United States , where he earned a BA in international relations at Brown University and an MBA at Harvard University . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;His Gojek , which began as a call center offering courier delivery and motorcycle taxi services and is now Indonesia 's first decacorn company , or a start-up valued at over US$10 billion , has made the young entrepreneur a household name particularly among the nation 's millennials. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Some educators believe Makarim 's extensive overseas learning may be an advantage as he seeks to map out what Indonesia , despite an impressive literacy rate of 99.6% , needs to do to match education standards in neighboring countries . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;With 64 million students , 340,000 schools and higher learning institutions and 3.9 million teachers and lecturers , Indonesia has the world 's fourth largest education system . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;figure id= " attachment408292 " style= " width : 1600px " class= " wp-caption alignnone " &gt;&lt;img class= " size-full wp-image-408292 " src= " https : **34;1113;TOOLONG ... alt= " " width= " 1600 " height= " 750 " srcset= " https : **31;1149;TOOLONG ... 1600w , https : **39;1182;TOOLONG ... 768w , https : **39;1223;TOOLONG ... 1568w " sizes= " ( max-width : 1600px ) 100vw , 1600px " /&gt;&lt;figcaption class= " wp-caption-text " &gt;Students in Indonesia lag their regional peers in standardized test results . Photo : **44;1264;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt;Financed by a 2019 budget of 152.6 trillion rupiah ( $10.8 billion ) , the amount represents only 3.5% of gross domestic product ( GDP ) compared to Vietnam 's 4.3% &amp;#8211 ; a nation which is taking the lion 's share of regional foreign direct investment ( FDI ) at a time when global supply chains are reconfiguring in response to the US-China trade war . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Those budgetary funds are clearly being misallocated . In the benchmark 2018 Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development 's ( OECD ) Program for Student Assessment ( PISA ) , 15-year-old Indonesian students finished 73rd in reading , 72nd in maths and 71st in science out of 79 countries surveyed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Indonesia 's aggregate score combining all three disciplines was 1,146 , representing just 78% of the OECD 's average and a decline of two percentage points over the previous survey in 2015 . More worrying , Indonesia ranked last in the percentage of employed adults with a tertiary degree . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;It has long been recognized that Indonesia 's education system is seriously flawed , with little improvement in quality made in the two decades since governments began devoting 20% of the national budget to a problem that is now widely seen as a major obstacle to national development . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Certain political analysts even suggest poor education lies at the heart of the country 's faltering progress towards democratization , a surfeit in learning that allows an unquestioning populace to be easily manipulated by self-interested politicians and their bureaucratic and corporate allies . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Makarim seems to agree with that assessment . " Every young person must be able to think independently , " he told Parliament 's education commission recently , stressing the need for a stronger connection between teachers , students and parents that technological advances in learning ca n't provide . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Before Makarim 's appointment , the education ministry 's top post was seemingly perpetually reserved for Muhammadiyah , the country 's second largest and mostly urban-based mass Muslim organization , which has done little over the years to meet the glaring need for reform . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;figure id= " attachment109751 " style= " width : 1600px " class= " wp-caption alignnone " &gt;&lt;img class= " size-full wp-image-109751 " src= " https : **34;1310;TOOLONG ... alt= " Indonesians share a computer . Photo : **42;1420;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt;Indonesian children may be starting school earlier and staying longer , but as former education minister Anies Baswedan pointed out in 2016 , the country is facing what he called an " education emergency , " beset by low-quality instruction , poor learning outcomes , inadequate facilities and discipline problems . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Siagian believes Makarim is on the right track with his decision to end the national examination in 2021 , and to retrain teachers in new classroom methods that earn them greater trust and allow schools the freedom to be more imaginative in their overall approach to education . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; " If they do that , they will overturn the apple cart , " he says , pointing to failed attempts in the past to find an alternative method of measuring academic accomplishment . " Kids will learn what is important instead of wasting their time having to memorize everything . " &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Makarim says he plans to replace the national exam with a so-called Assessment of Minimum Competency and Survey of Character , but he has made it clear it will not be used to measure a student 's eligibility to move to the next grade . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;That will fall to the National Standard School Examination ( USBN ) , managed only by schools and built around written tests or other more comprehensive exercises that will give teachers and schools greater freedom in evaluating learning outcomes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Siagian contends that too many outside vested interests are involved in Indonesia 's education system , ranging from the military to the printing industry , the latter of which benefits from lucrative examination paper and textbook contracts . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Andrew Rosser , a Melbourne University political economist , laid out a crushing indictment of those same outside influences in a 2018 Lowy Institute paper that is now viewed as an empirical work on the problems afflicting Indonesian education . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Rather than producing Indonesians capable of finding jobs and other opportunities in the global economy , he wrote , " their interests have been in the development of an education system that helps them to accumulate resources , distribute patronage , mobilize political support and exercise political control . &lt;p&gt;It is that &amp;#8211 ; and the questionable ability of teachers to adapt &amp;#8211 ; that will present Makarim with his biggest challenges in 2020 and beyond . &lt;/p&gt; Avangard hypersonic missile can carry a 2-megaton nuclear weapon at speeds that make it ' invulnerable to interception ' &gt;https : **33;1660;TOOLONG ... has deployed its first hypersonic nuclear-capable missiles , with Vladimir Putin boasting that it puts his country in a class of its own . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;According to a report in The Guardian , the president described the Avangard hypersonic glide vehicle , which can fly at 27 times the speed of sound , as a technological breakthrough comparable to the 1957 Soviet launch of the first satellite . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Putin has said Russia 's new generation of nuclear weapons can hit almost any point in the world and evade a US-built missile shield , though some western experts have questioned how advanced some of the weapons programs are . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The Avangard is launched on top of an intercontinental ballistic missile , but , unlike a regular missile warhead , which follows a predictable path after separation , it can make sharp manoeuvres en route to its target , making it harder to intercept . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The defence minister , Sergei Shoigu , told Putin the first missile unit equipped with the Avangard had entered combat duty . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; " I congratulate you on this landmark event for the military and the entire nation , " Shoigu said later during a conference call with top military leaders . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The strategic missile forces chief , Gen Sergei Karakaev , said during the call that the Avangard had been put on duty with a unit in the Orenburg region in the southern Ural mountains . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Putin unveiled the Avangard and other prospective weapons systems in his state-of-the-nation address in March 2018 , saying its ability to make sharp manoeuvres on its way to a target would render missile defense useless . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; " It heads to target like a meteorite , like a fireball , " he said at the time . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The Russian leader said the Avangard had been designed using new composite materials to withstand temperatures of up to 2,000C ( 3,632F ) which can be reached while travelling at hypersonic speeds . &lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt; -- AFP&lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt; Philippines ' military is looking for a generational replacement for an aerial workhorse which has served them for decades &gt;https : **33;3318;TOOLONG ... the Cold War , Soviet aircraft were a top concern for the Philippine Air Force until 1990 . The Unites States and the Philippines remain allies under a 1951 mutual defense treaty . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;However , President Rodrigo Duterte , has pursued a foreign policy aimed at balancing relationships in the Indo-Pacific area . &lt;p&gt;The storm , with wind gusts of up to 200 kilometers , or 124 miles , per hour , swept across remote villages and popular tourist destinations in the central Philippines on Wednesday . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Authorities on Friday confirmed 28 people had died , up from 16 on Thursday , as information came in from badly hit areas where internet and mobile phone networks had been cut . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;&amp;#8220 ; We&amp;#8217 ; re hoping against it , &amp;#8221 ; said national disaster agency spokesman Mark Timbal. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;He said at least 12 people were still listed as missing . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Among those killed were several members of a family who drowned , a policeman electrocuted by a toppled post while patrolling and a man struck by a felled coconut tree . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The Philippines is a mostly Catholic nation , and Phanfone ruined or disrupted Christmas festivities for hundreds of thousands of people . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The typhoon displaced tens of thousands living on the coast and low-lying areas who were forced to celebrate Christmas in evacuation centers. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Others missed family reunions , with plane and ferry services canceled. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;It also hit Boracay island , famed for its white-sand beaches which draw more than one million tourists a year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Coconut trees were uprooted on Boracay and windows in some resorts were blown in during the storm , and ferry services to and from the island were cut on Wednesday and Thursday . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;However , no one died on Boracay , and the damage was not on the scale of badly hit coastal towns elsewhere in the central Philippines . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The Philippines is the first major landmass facing the Pacific typhoon belt and is hit by an average of about 20 storms a year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Phanfone , locally named &amp;#8220 ; Ursula , &amp;#8221 ; &lt;p&gt;Though much weaker , Phanfone tracked a similar path as Super Typhoon Haiyan -- the country&amp;#8217 ; s deadliest storm on record which left more than 7,300 people dead or missing in 2013. &lt;/p&gt; Thanks to director Sam Mendes&amp;#8217 ; ham-handed attempts at cinematic innovation , the audience views the sequence of events from the perspective of a small dog dragged along on a leash behind them . The film , which opened on Christmas Day in the United States , leaves the audience with no more understanding of war or the men who fight it than a canine mascot must acquire . &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p class= " p1 " &gt;&lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;The &lt;a href= " https : **33;7026;TOOLONG ... film&lt;/a&gt; has many virtues , or rather qualities which would have been virtues had they been in a different film . It offers superb acting and no-expense-spared sets and effect , but its strengths are vitiated by a wrongheaded conception of cinematic time . &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p class= " p1 " &gt;&lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;Mendes and his crew made enormous efforts to film as much of the action as possible in continuous shots , where the camera follows the actors for a lengthy interval , as they explained in a 12-minute " making of **25;7061;TOOLONG " &lt;span class= " s2 " **27;7088;TOOLONG . The camera trails the actors in what Mendes imagines to be " real time " through trenches , battlefields , ruined cities , and assorted disasters . Technically this poses great challenges , but the aesthetic outcome is a canine perspective on human events . &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;&lt;iframe width= " 640 " height= " 360 " src= " https : **33;7117;TOOLONG ... frameborder= " 0 " allow= " accelerometer ; autoplay ; encrypted-media ; gyroscope ; picture-in-picture " **44;7152;TOOLONG &lt;p class= " p1 " &gt;&lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;Time is represented as an indifferent sequence of moments , which means practically that every moment commands equal attention . In this nightmarish world there can be no drama , that is , no climax . On the contrary , every occurrence of importance to the thin narrative necessarily becomes an anti-climax . &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p class= " p1 " &gt;&lt;span class= " s1 " &gt; The effect is queasiness , similar to the experience of certain virtual reality videos . When you leap into virtual space or drive a virtual race car while wearing a VR headset , the cognitive dissonance between your artificial perception of motion and your stationary body makes you dizzy . It is of clinical interest that a similar effect is produced by moving through an endless blah of cinematic time , stumbling from moment to moment without direction or purpose . &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p class= " p1 " &gt;&lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;The barebones plot sadly reinforces the sense of temporal disorientation . Two corporals ( Dean-Charles Chapman and George MacKay ) are dispatched to warn a British division against charging into a German trap . They walk past piles of corpses in shell craters , through abandoned but booby-trapped German trenches , and ruined villages . In the midst of their journey , a German plane is shot down . They rescue the pilot from the burning aircraft , but he stabs one of them to death . The surviving corporal makes his way past German stragglers to the British lines , and with heroic effort persuades the commanding officer to call off the attack . The officer ( Benedict Cumberbatch ) comments cynically that today he has been ordered to stand down , but next week it will be " attack at dawn . " &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p class= " p1 " &gt;&lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;Fever nightmares that drag on interminably convey a similar effect . Although **25;7198;TOOLONG has been compared to Steven Spielberg 's &lt;em&gt;Saving Private Ryan&lt;/em&gt; ( 1998 ) , the resemblance is entirely superficial . In the 1998 film , a squad is dispatched on a humanitarian mission to find a soldier who has just lost three brothers in combat . The Spielberg film , one of the best war films ever made , asks viewers to consider the value of a single human life : Is it worth sacrificing the lives of several men for the life of one , even under exceptional circumstances ? " Ryan " does not offer an easy answer . &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p class= " p1 " &gt;&lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;What separates " Ryan " from **25;7225;TOOLONG is cinematic time . Spielberg 's film is shown from the perspective of the now-elderly Ryan visiting the grave of the captain who died saving him , wondering whether the life he has lived has been good enough to redeem the sacrifice . Spielberg well understands that our perception of time is not linear . Time is not a succession of indifferent moments ( except perhaps to Schopenhauer ) , but a composite created by human reflection . This was first stated clearly by St Augustine in &lt;em&gt;The Confessions&lt;/em&gt; : the past is gone , the present moment is too insubstantial to grasp , and the future has not yet arrived . Past , present and future therefore can not be perceived directly . What we call time arises from our own reflection . It is a composite of memory and anticipation . &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/p&gt; &lt;p class= " p1 " &gt;&lt;span class= " s1 " &gt;What makes " Ryan " an effective work of art ( and not merely a lesson in morality ) is Spielberg 's cinematic ability to evoke reflection in time . Earlier this year , Infantino had suggested that North and South Korea should prepare a joint bid to host the 2023 Women&amp;#8217 ; s World Cup . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;But as he closes in on the venue -- an area that should be bustling -- Infantino gets a sense that something is not right . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;When he enters the VIP box and looks out over the stadium , with its 50,000 red , white and blue seats , he realizes why . Bar a few officials and Pyongyang-based diplomats , the only spectators for this landmark game are the FIFA president and his entourage . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Kim Il Sung stadium is empty . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;figure id= " attachment407823 " style= " width : 1024px " class= " wp-caption alignnone " &gt;&lt;img class= " size-full wp-image-407823 " src= " https : **34;7847;TOOLONG ... alt= " " width= " 1024 " height= " 768 " srcset= " https : **31;7883;TOOLONG ... 1024w , https : **39;7916;TOOLONG ... 768w " sizes= " ( max-width : 1024px ) 100vw , 1024px " /&gt;&lt;figcaption class= " wp-caption-text " &gt;The North Korea-South Korea World Cup qualification match about to get underway at Kim Il Sung Stadium in Pyongyang . The roar of the non-existent crowd is slightly less than thunderous . Photo : **41;7957;TOOLONG &lt;h4&gt;Football diplomacy&lt;/h4&gt; &lt;p&gt;The bizarre outcome had been a long time coming . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;In July 2019 , at the headquarters of the Asian Football Confederation ( AFC ) in Kuala Lumpur , the draws were made for the World Cup 2022 qualifying groups . To great excitement , North and South Korea ended up together in Group H. The North was scheduled to host the first match . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;But whether the match could take place in Pyongyang remained to be seen . Apart from a friendly in 1990 , all official matches between the two Koreas were played outside North Korea . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Still , the year is different . The relationship between North and South has improved massively since early 2018 , when , in a last-moment initiative , Pyongyang sent athletes to the Winter Olympics in Pyeongchang , South Korea . During the opening ceremony , athletes of both Koreas entered the stadium together under the Unification Flag . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Soon after , North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and South Korean President Moon Jae-in held a summit in the Demilitarized Zone . Those developments led to the historic summit in Singapore between Kim and US President Donald Trump . Only a few months earlier , the two leaders had been engaged in a high-tension war of words that many feared would escalate into the real thing . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;At a second summit in Hanoi , negotiations broke down , but in June the two leaders met for a third time at the DMZ -- and Trump became the first US president to set foot in North Korea , very briefly . The two agreed to quickly resume negotiations . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;In July , the North Korean Football Association ( PRKFA ) announced the game would take place on October 15 at 5.30pm. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h4&gt;'Nothing certain ' &lt;/h4&gt; &lt;p&gt;Simon Cockerell , general manager of Beijing-based Koryo Tours , a travel company specializing in trips to North Korea , is marketing a special football trip to Pyongyang . As well as the match , participants will visit the DMZ and a catfish farm . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; " I thought it a reasonable assumption that the match would be held , " Cockerell tells Asia Times . &amp;#8220 ; But I told customers that nothing is guaranteed . In North Korea , nothing is certain . " &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;South Korea 's Ministry of Unification hopefully sees the match as an opportunity to improve relations with the North . Ever since the failed summit in Hanoi , Pyongyang has slowed cooperation with Seoul . When Seoul offered Pyongyang 50,000 tons of rice to help the millions of underfed citizens , it is refused . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Ministry officials approach their counterparts at the joint Liaison Office , established in 2018 , inside North Korea near the border city of Kaesong . Officials of both Koreas meet here twice a day , but for months , little substantive has been discussed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The Southerners request visas for fans and journalists , and ask if the South 's team can travel the 120 miles from Seoul to Pyongyang overland . Normally , travelers to North Korea arrive via Beijing , where the North Korean embassy distributes visas . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The North Koreans do n't reply . " There was no chance for us to talk with the North on this issue , " a spokesperson from the ministry told Asia Times . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The ministry asks the South Korean Football Association ( KFA ) to assist . A KFA official consults with his counterpart in Pyongyang , via email , about practical matters like accommodation , food and training times . They copy FIFA and the AFC on every email . But when asked about visas , the PRKFA official says it is " not his decision . " &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The North Koreans clearly have no intention of cooperating on the matter of fans and reporters . FIFA intervenes . Still , the North does not budge . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h4&gt;Vexation , frustration&lt;/h4&gt; &lt;p&gt;The South Koreans comfort themselves that they will at least have the opportunity to see the game live on television . Public broadcaster KBS is negotiating with the North 's state broadcaster through a third party in Japan . A contract has been signed and KBS has paid the North Koreans a deposit of $300,000. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;A few days before the game , the North Koreans end talks . " They are smart , " a KFA official says . " They did the absolute minimum necessary to organize the game , but nothing more . " &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Why ? Experts point out that while Kim Jong-un wields absolute power in North Korea , different sections within the state and the party compete for power and influence . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; " There is not one brain deciding what happens there , " a source who visits North Korea regularly told Asia Times . " It is entirely possible that the Football Association was allowed to organize the match because the promotion of sport is important , but later got overruled by another more powerful department that said security was more important . " &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;And Pyongyang is unhappy . North Korea wants South Korea to engage in commercial tourism and logistics projects in the North , but Seoul is trammeled by international sanctions . Meanwhile , critical talks between Pyongyang and Washington on denuclearization have broken down . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;That is the political background . However , none of this affected the South 's game preparation . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h4&gt;Match prep&lt;/h4&gt; &lt;p&gt;South Korea 's national team is trying not be distracted . Portuguese coach Paulo Bento says he is unafraid of facing a stadium packed with 50,000 fanatical home team supporters . " Professional athletes would all want to compete before huge crowds , " he says . " I don&amp;#8217 ; t think our players will be fired up to play at an empty stadium . " &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Seoul 's Ministry of Unification announces some good news : The North promises to provide a DVD of the game . KBS announces a broadcast for the day the team returns to Seoul . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;South Korean fans wave the national team goodbye at the airport . The North never replied to the request to travel overland , so the team flies to Beijing , where they stay overnight to await visas . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;In Beijing , staff and players leave their phones at the South Korean embassy . " If a phone got stolen or hacked , that would lead to a whole new set of problems , " a source close to the team told Asia Times . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;On the morning of the game , North Korean officials announce that all tickets are sold . " There were several indications that the stadium would be full , " according to a FIFA spokesman . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;But during their warm-up , the South Koreans are sensing something is odd . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; " I asked if something was wrong , but got no answer , " says a source close to the team . " We decided to concentrate on the match . " &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Tour operator Simon Cockerell is in Pyongyang with eight tourists who signed up specifically for the football trip . They get nowhere . " I was truly amazed , " he said . " And after so many trips to the North I have a high bar of being amazed . " &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h4&gt;No goals&lt;/h4&gt; &lt;p&gt;Inside the huge stadium , there is no crowd and no TV crews -- only two teams , on the pitch . Then kick-off and the match begins . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;It is only thanks to Swedish Ambassador Joachim Bergstr ? m , that the outside world sees anything of the game . Bergstr ? m , a few meters away from the FIFA president in the VIP box , shares several images and videos of the match on Twitter . The pictures show stewards -- soldiers , judging by their outfits -- facing the stands , despite the lack of spectators . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The game ends in a goalless draw . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;That 's a good result for North Korea -- number 116 in FIFA rankings , far below South Korea 's 41st place . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;North Korea 's official KCNA news agency issues a brief report saying the qualifier ended in a 0-0 draw after a series of " attacks and counter-attacks. " &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;It is the only line the North Korean regime communicates about the game . According to specialist media NK News , almost no one in Pyongyang is aware that a match that could have been historic had even taken place . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;figure id= " attachment407821 " style= " width : 433px " class= " wp-caption alignnone " &gt;&lt;img class= " size-full wp-image-407821 " src= " https : **34;8000;TOOLONG ... alt= " " width= " 433 " height= " 577 " /&gt;&lt;figcaption class= " wp-caption-text " &gt;Security guards keep a watchful eye over the non-existent crowd at Kim Il Sung stadium . Photo : **41;8036;TOOLONG &lt;h4&gt;Leaving unscathed&lt;/h4&gt; &lt;p&gt;Gutted , Infantino requests an explanation from North Korean officials . He receives no reply . The same night , &lt;a href= " https : **33;8079;TOOLONG ... sends out a press release full of frustration . &lt;/a&gt; " I was looking forward to seeing a full stadium for such a historic match but was disappointed to see there were no fans in the stands , " he writes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Technically speaking , North Korea violated only one FIFA rule : Every host country has to accept foreign journalists . " Freedom of the press and freedom of speech are obviously paramount , " Infantino writes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;A host country is also obliged to allow spectators , but in this case North Korea can argue that there were spectators -- officials in the VIP box . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;FIFA later decides not to discipline North Korea . However , chances are slim that the country will be asked any time soon to organize a big sporting event , like the Women 's World Cup . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Two days after the game , South Korea 's players return home . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Captain Son Heung-min -- Tottenham Hotspur 's star striker -- complains about a " rough " game . " The opponents were pretty physical , and we exchanged some terse words , " Son told South Korean reporters . " Rather than focusing on the match , we started worrying about trying not to get hurt . It means a lot to have come out unscathed . " &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h4&gt;World unchanged&lt;/h4&gt; &lt;p&gt;Last hopes are soon dashed . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Immediately after landing , KFA officials use a mobile DVD player to check the contents of the recording they received . The video of the game is poor quality -- unfit for broadcast . KBS cancels its planned broadcast . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;In response to demand , the KFA organizes a limited viewing at its headquarters . Press agency Yonhap concludes that South Korean players " had trouble establishing themselves on offense against their hard-nosed opponents . " &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The North Koreans stay quiet . A month afterwards , however , foreign diplomats in Pyongyang receive a warning to " stop sharing sensitive photos and video on their social media accounts with ' impure intentions , ' " NK News reports . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Since then , Ambassador Bergstr ? m has gone quiet on Twitter . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The optimistic Moon has made North-South relations his presidential flagship policy , but after the match , it is clear that Seoul is frustrated . Very frustrated . The KFA sends an official complaint to FIFA , then , in mid-December , Seoul withdraws from the bidding process for the 2023 Women 's World Cup , shooting down Infantino&amp;#8217 ; s plan for a precedent-busting North-South hosting . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The FIFA president , who left Pyongyang by private jet directly after the game , has remained quiet since penning his statement . Still , one can sense the sports leader 's frustration . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; " It would be na ? ve to think we can change the world from one minute to the next , " he wrote . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;&lt;em&gt;This article first appeared in Dutch newspaper &lt;span class= " gmaildefault " &gt;De Volkskrant&lt;/span&gt; . It is exclusively reprinted in English by Asia Times with the writer&amp;#8217 ; s permission . &lt;/em&gt;&lt;/p&gt; Police and pro-democracy protesters clash inside shopping malls as chief executive said Christmas had been ' ruined ' &gt;https : **33;8114;TOOLONG ... class= " txt-textContent " &gt; &lt;div class= " text fontsize0 jqContent jqlangdir " &gt; &lt;p&gt;Hong Kong endured a third straight day of political unrest over the Christmas period Thursday as police and pro-democracy protesters clashed inside shopping malls. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Protesters spent the afternoon on Thursday marching through multiple malls chanting anti-government and anti-police slogans . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Riot police swooped on dozens of black-clad protesters in one mall in Tai Po district , using pepper spray as well as blue dye to mark suspects , said a reporter on the scene . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Police made multiple arrests . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Hong Kong has been battered by more than six months of protests that has upended the financial hub&amp;#8217 ; s reputation for stability and helped tip the city into recession . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The city&amp;#8217 ; s many malls have become regular protest venues as demonstrators try to cause economic disruption and pressure the city&amp;#8217 ; s pro-Beijing leadership . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The last month had seen a relative drop-off in violence and protests after pro-democracy candidates won a landslide at local elections . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;But with Beijing and city leaders refusing further concessions , rallies and clashes have reignited over the Christmas period . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;h4&gt;&amp;#8216 ; Ruined&amp;#8217 ; Christmas&lt;/h4&gt; &lt;p&gt;Christmas Eve saw some of the worst violence in weeks as protesters and police fought running battles for hours in a busy shopping district . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Sporadic and less severe clashes broke out again inside malls on Christmas Day . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;On Wednesday , Hong Kong&amp;#8217 ; s pro-Beijing leader Carrie Lam said violent protesters had &amp;#8220 ; ruined&amp;#8221 ; Christmas . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Protest groups counter that they have been left with little choice but to return to the streets because Beijing and Lam continue to dig their heels in. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Swathes of the population are seething against Beijing&amp;#8217 ; s rule and the semi-autonomous city&amp;#8217 ; s administration as they push for greater democratic freedoms and police accountability . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The protests were initially sparked by a now-abandoned attempt to allow extraditions to the authoritarian mainland . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;They have since morphed into a popular revolt against Beijing&amp;#8217 ; s rule , with spiraling fears that the city is losing some of its unique liberties . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Among the demands being made by protesters are an inquiry into the police , an amnesty for the more than 6,000 people arrested and the right to elect Hong Kong&amp;#8217 ; s leader . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; -- **34;8149;TOOLONG &lt;/div&gt; &lt;/div&gt; Will it be another turbulent year for the territory ? There are three key things to watch &gt;https : **33;8185;TOOLONG ... one could have envisaged that a love story that ended in murder in Taipei in February 2018 would trigger the worst-ever maelstrom to engulf Hong Kong and alter the course of the city&amp;#8217 ; s politics for good . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Nor could Carrie Lam have ever imagined that her ingenuity in using the case -- a Hongkonger who strangled his girlfriend and fled back to the city but could not be rendered to Taiwan to stand trial -- as a pretext for ramming through new legislation allowing extradition to not only Taiwan but also mainland China would forsake all her political capital and even her career as the top leader of the territory . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;figure id= " attachment407802 " style= " width : 892px " class= " wp-caption aligncenter " &gt;&lt;img class= " size-full wp-image-407802 " src= " https : **34;8220;TOOLONG ... alt= " " width= " 892 " height= " 593 " srcset= " https : **31;8256;TOOLONG ... 892w , https : **39;8289;TOOLONG ... 768w " sizes= " ( max-width : 892px ) 100vw , 892px " /&gt;&lt;figcaption class= " wp-caption-text " &gt;Anti-extradition bill protesters throng a main thoroughfare amid clouds of tear gas near Hong Kong&amp;#8217 ; s government headquarters in the city&amp;#8217 ; s Admiralty district . Photo : **44;8330;TOOLONG &; ... &lt;p&gt;As the unrest seethes for the sixth straight month in the former British colony , the local government has , in this otherwise festive period , canceled the traditional New Year&amp;#8217 ; s Eve fireworks gala in Victoria Harbor and other extravaganzas and urged people to instead stay indoors , while mustering constables to patrol and lockdown streets and protest hotspots to keep troublemakers at bay . But not too many are bothered , since the protest-weary city is in no mood for celebrations anyway , with many agonizing about another eventful year ahead . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Will Hong Kong hurtle from one turbulent year to another ? What is in store for 2020 ? There are three things to watch . &lt;/p&gt; **25;8376;TOOLONG . Legislative Council **34;8403;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt;A majority of the seats in the city&amp;#8217 ; s legislature will be up for grabs in a citywide , high-stakes poll to be held in September 2020. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The pro-Beijing bloc has to erase the ignominy of the crushing rout in November&amp;#8217 ; s district council election when it lost the monopoly of positions to the pan-democratic camp as most of its incumbent councilors were booted out . This is because Hongkongers&amp;#8217 ; uproar against the now-retracted extradition bill and alleged police brutality turned into votes for the opposition . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;figure id= " attachment407800 " style= " width : 889px " class= " wp-caption aligncenter " &gt;&lt;img class= " size-full wp-image-407800 " src= " https : **34;8439;TOOLONG ... alt= " " width= " 889 " height= " 592 " srcset= " https : **31;8475;TOOLONG ... 889w , https : **39;8508;TOOLONG ... 768w " sizes= " ( max-width : 889px ) 100vw , 889px " /&gt;&lt;figcaption class= " wp-caption-text " &gt;Hong Kong protesters storm the Legislative Council and occupy the assembly hall to protest against a controversial extradition bill on July 1 , on the 22nd anniversary of the territory&amp;#8217 ; s handover from Britain to China . The now-pulled extradition bill was intended to allow the surrender of fugitives to mainland China and other jurisdictions that do not have any rendition deals with the city . Photo : **43;8700;TOOLONG &g; ... &lt;p&gt;Embattled Beijing loyalists will have to fight a treacherous battle in the LegCo election to defend their majority , under the imperative from up north that the legislature must remain pliant to endorse bills tabled by the government . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The opposition , meanwhile , is set to clinch another neat win if the poll is to be held right away , and analysts say the camp as a whole may indeed garner a higher voter turnout as unlike selecting district councilors who mainly deal with livelihood issues , the LegCo election is laden with politics . And for the first time in the territory&amp;#8217 ; s history , pan-dems may even grab more than 35 of the 70 seats to effectively put a straitjacket on the government with their vetoing power . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;What remains to be seen is how the protracted political crisis will evolve or be defused in the new year , and if more voters will be galvanized to strengthen the base of the opposition should the government continue to shun the common demands from protesters -- ranging from universal suffrage to probing police brutality . &lt;/p&gt; **25;8745;TOOLONG . National security **37;8772;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt;The outcome of the LegCo election will be consequential for Beijing&amp;#8217 ; s rumored fresh bid to enact Article 23 ( national security ) of the Basic Law , the city&amp;#8217 ; s constitutional document , and that is why Beijing and its subordinates in the city are getting antsy . A two-thirds majority is needed once a major bill is put to a vote at the legislature . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The legislation of this particular article , which outlaws treason , secession , sedition and subversion against the central authorities , theft of state secrets , as well as foreign political organizations conducting activities and establishing ties with local entities , was deferred after a failed attempt in 2003 that drove half a million people into the streets and led to the early departure of the city&amp;#8217 ; s first post-colonial leader . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Local papers cite pro-establishment politicos as saying that Beijing had already mandated the article to be passed by the end of 2020 provided that its loyalists could retain the majority inside the Legco chamber , as Beijing rejigs its policies to quell the unrest . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;figure id= " attachment366844 " style= " width : 653px " class= " wp-caption aligncenter " &gt;&lt;img class= " size-full wp-image-366844 " src= " https : **34;8811;TOOLONG ... alt= " " width= " 653 " height= " 398 " /&gt;&lt;figcaption class= " wp-caption-text " &gt;China 's national emblem hanging at the main entrance of Beijing 's liaison office in Hong Kong is defaced by protesters during a rally in July . Photo : WikiMedia/Studio **41;9148;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt;These reports claim that Chinese President Xi Jinping had handed down his latest decree to Carrie Lam , Hong Kong&amp;#8217 ; s beleaguered chief executive , to enact Article 23 before the end of her tenure , when the latter was summoned for a duty visit to Beijing earlier this month . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The need for such legislation is exigent to thwart the meddling of the West in Hong Kong amid Beijing&amp;#8217 ; s steady diet of such allegations since the outbreak of the protests . Furthermore , top cadres are said to believe that when the situation in the city had already hit rock bottom , there would be no need to wait for a more &amp;#8220 ; ripe&amp;#8221 ; time but should enact the article once and for all . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Also , Lam is unlikely to seek another term beyond 2022 , making her an ideal leader &amp;#8220 ; with nothing to lose&amp;#8221 ; to press ahead with such an unpopular task when any leader counting on a popular mandate would skulk away from the job . Lam was praised for her &amp;#8220 ; iron-fisted resolve and loyalty&amp;#8221 ; by Xi when the latter was briefed in &lt;a href= " https : **33;9191;TOOLONG ... **25;9226;TOOLONG . Lam&amp;#8217 ; s **35;9253;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt;As the least popular leader Hong Kong has ever seen , Lam&amp;#8217 ; s days in office are numbered . She is loathed by residents and blamed by Beijing loyalists for their electoral defeats . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;She may bow out as Tung Chee-hwa did : He offered to step down in March 2005 , citing the debilitating impact of heavy work on&lt;span class= " Apple-converted-space " &gt; his &lt;/span&gt;health , after a public dress-down by Chinese leaders , less than two years after the failure to pass Article 23. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;figure id= " attachment101136 " style= " width : 3130px " class= " wp-caption aligncenter " &gt;&lt;img class= " size-full wp-image-101136 " src= " https : **34;9290;TOOLONG ... alt= " Carrie Lam , Chief Executive of Hong Kong . Photo : Reuters " width= " 3130 " height= " 2071 " srcset= " https : **31;9326;TOOLONG ... 3130w , https : **39;9359;TOOLONG ... 580w " sizes= " ( max-width : 3130px ) 100vw , 3130px " /&gt;&lt;figcaption class= " wp-caption-text " &gt;Carrie Lam&amp;#8217 ; s days in office are numbered . These gigs pay less , offer fewer benefits and less security than formal ones . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;That they 're overwhelmingly going to women belies the spin about Japan 's other half getting ahead . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;For all of Abe 's successes in strengthening corporate governance , Japan Inc has yet to embrace the meritocratic mores that drive hiring decisions in the West . Seniority-based promotions are still the norm . There are far more Chinese than Russians in that vast , underpopulated neighborhood , and Beijing reckons the Tsars stole the territory in the first place . &lt;/p&gt; **25;10942;TOOLONG ; s game&lt;/h4&gt; &lt;p&gt;While China has slim prospects for breaking through the East China Sea island barriers , Beijing is persistent and patient . China this month rolled out its first locally built aircraft carrier and is building high-quality ships and aircraft at a rapid clip . It out-built the US Navy by a 4:1 ratio over the last decade . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Regionally , it has perhaps 10 times more ships available than the US Navy 's **26;10969;TOOLONG Fleet . And do n't forget China 's Coast Guard , law enforcement ships and so-called maritime militia -- its weaponized fishing fleet . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Looking ahead , do the math . The US either builds a lot more ships -- and fast -- or gets its regional partners better organized and armed . Ideally , both . Will that happen in 2020 ? No. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;And Beijing is looking toward distant horizons . It has spent 30 years insinuating itself into the economies , societies and political leadership of Central Pacific states -- Micronesia , Marshall Islands , Kiribati , Palau -- and even US territories of Northern Marianas and Guam . And it has stepped up efforts in recent years in the South Pacific . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;China has not made military inroads -- yet . Those will come later . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Currently , Beijing is leaning on the Philippines , and upping its game in the South China Sea , to outflank Taiwan . The matter is not decided , however . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Next year will see continued Chinese efforts to chisel away at Taiwan , Japan and South Korea . Chisel long enough and , one day , something gives . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;That wo n't happen in 2020 . However , in the 42 years since I started as a Pyongyang watcher , I&amp;#8217 ; ve found that the thinking of the ruling Kims and their minions is far from impenetrable. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The basic lesson from those decades of close study is that this is a regime that has its own ways , different from others&amp;#8217 ; ways -- and has no wish or intention to change much . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The regime&amp;#8217 ; s unusual ways are tied directly to certain goals . Unchallenged domination of current US ally South Korea tops Pyongyang&amp;#8217 ; s wishlist . That&amp;#8217 ; s something the North expects to have a better shot at achieving after a first step : persuading Trump to withdraw US troops and sign a peace treaty formally ending the Korean War . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Optimists have popped up with considerable frequency since the 1970s in the United States , South Korea and elsewhere to predict big changes in Pyongyang&amp;#8217 ; s ways and , particularly , its goals . Sooner or later , they have always been proven wrong . There is not now and there never will be a kinder , gentler North Korea ruled by the Kim family . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;With that in mind , it is as clear as day that Kim Jong Un considers 2020 his year to remove American constraints on his power . And that&amp;#8217 ; s the meaning of the end-of-the-year , fish-or-cut-bait deadline he delivered months ago to Donald Trump . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Why did he allow all that time , instead of demanding quicker results ? For one thing , it gave the North Koreans an opportunity to put in incremental work improving their weapons systems . That&amp;#8217 ; s been easy for them to manage . Pressure to do otherwise , from enemies and allies alike , fell away largely on account of Kim&amp;#8217 ; s charm offensive and his public bromance with Trump . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;But the main reason Kim chose the end of 2019 for his deadline is , simply put , that he reads Trump . He knows that once the election campaign year has begun the US president and chief Artist of The Deal will be more amenable than ever to giving up the store , in the hope a bad deal can be passed off as good to enough voters for him to get re-elected . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Pyongyang will have only the one reelection year , with its maximum opportunity to entrap Trump -- unless the highly self-regarding president wins reelection and then figures a way to realize his dream of abolishing the two-term limit on presidents . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;One benefit of not having changed the system appreciably over the 70-odd years of the North Korean regime&amp;#8217 ; s existence is that officials who&amp;#8217 ; ve managed to avoid the firing squad have tended to stick around for long periods and develop great familiarity with their jobs . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Take Kim Yong Nam . He already was in charge of studying the US enemy way back in 1979 when I met him for lunch in Pyongyang and we talked for five hours . Old Kim ( no close relation the ruling family ) did finally retire this year , at 91 . But there are plenty of other , somewhat younger people , with decades of US-watching experience , who remain to make sure the latest Kim ruler reads the enemy correctly . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Trump&amp;#8217 ; s and Kim&amp;#8217 ; s denuclearization &amp;#8220 ; process , &amp;#8221 ; such as it was , pretty much halted when a second summit early this year in Hanoi collapsed . I&amp;#8217 ; m not going to endorse unseen whatever his current prescription might be , in case it&amp;#8217 ; s hot war he has in mind . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Still , policies that I think must be considered include some that are only somewhat less martial than actually dropping bombs . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Following the Cold War playbook by upping the deterrent level may , conceivably , end up being the last and best North Korea option for the United States -- and for any allies that stand with the US rather than giving in to what may seem , particularly with Trump in the White House , the inevitability of Kimdom . ( I&amp;#8217 ; m looking especially at you , President Moon Jae-in. ) &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Sound policy may conceivably involve accepting ( even encouraging ) the rise of two new nuclear powers , South Korea and Japan . That would be bad , of course , in proliferation terms . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;But in the grand scheme of things it could turn out better than giving in to Kim&amp;#8217 ; s dreams of extending his family&amp;#8217 ; s rule over the proud industrialized democracy that now exists south of the Demilitarized Zone . &lt;/p&gt; **26;12705;TOOLONG Asia-focused journalist Bradley K. She added lights to her Christmas-themed ornaments . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/div&gt; &lt;div class= " text en " &gt; &lt;p&gt;&amp;#8220 ; We didn&amp;#8217 ; t have this technology before , &amp;#8221 ; she said . &amp;#8220 ; We only had plastic or fiberglass ornaments . &amp;#8221 ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;/div&gt; &lt;/div&gt; &lt;/div&gt; &lt;/div&gt; &lt;/div&gt; USAF will request eight Advanced Eagle F-15X fighters in its budget , with plans to buy 80 fighters over five years &gt;https : **33;12768;TOOLONG ... nearly three decades , the F-15 Eagle fighter was considered the undisputed king of the skies . Until the debut of its replacement , the F-22 Raptor , the F-15 was the US Air Force 's frontline air superiority fighter . Even today , a modernized Eagle is still considered a formidable opponent , and manufacturer Boeing has proposed updated versions that could keep the airframe flying for the better part of a century . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;According to a special report by Kyle Mizokami , in The National Interest , the F-15 traces its roots to the air war in Vietnam , and the inauspicious showing of American Air Force and Navy fighters versus their North Korean counterparts . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Large , powerful American fighters , designed to tackle both air-to-air and air-to-ground missions , were performing poorly against their smaller , less powerful -- but more maneuverable -- North Vietnamese counterparts . The 13:1 kill ratio American fliers enjoyed in the Korean War dropped to an abysmal 1.5 to 1 kill ratio in Vietnam . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Contemporary fighters , such as the F-4 Phantom , had been designed under the assumption that the air-to-air missile had rendered dogfights obsolete , and with them the need for superiority maneuverability and a gun for air combat . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The USAF decided it needed a dedicated air superiority fighter , one that combined two powerful engines , a powerful radar , a large number of missiles &lt;em&gt;and&lt;/em&gt; a gun . Above all , it had to be maneuverable enough to win a dogfight. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The Air Force issued a request for proposals for the new FX fighter in 1966 , and no fewer than six companies submitted competing paper designs . No prototypes were built . The air service selected McDonnell Douglas ( now a part of Boeing ) in 1969 , ordering 107 full-scale development planes . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The F-15 was a formidable aircraft . Early versions were powered by two Pratt &amp;amp ; Whitney F100-PW-100 after-burning turbofan engines , producing 14,500 pounds of static thrust -- 23,500 with afterburners. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;This gave the aircraft a thrust-to-weight ratio of greater than one , making it so powerful that it was the first fighter to exceed the speed of sound in vertical flight . The F-15 had so much thrust it could climb to sixty-five thousand feet in just 122 seconds . In horizontal flight , the F-15 could reach speeds of Mach 2.5 , and cruise at speeds of Mach 0.9. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The Eagle 's AN/APG-63 nose mounted radar was the most advanced of its day , a solid state radar with " look down/shoot down " capability and a range of up to 200 miles . This allowed the F-15 to pick out low-flying enemies on radar against the clutter generated by the ground . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The radar was also the first to incorporate a programmable system processor , which allowed moderate upgrades to be done via software and not intrusive hardware updates . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The Eagle was originally armed with four radar-guided AIM-7 Sparrow missiles for long-range engagements and four AIM-9 Sidewinder infrared guided missiles for short-range engagements . In the air war over Vietnam , USAF F-4C Phantoms , lacking a dedicated gun , missed several opportunities to down enemy aircraft . This was remedied in the F-15 by equipping the plane with an internal M61 Vulcan 20mm gatling gun . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The F-15 was also designed with long range in mind . Carrying three six-hundred-pound fuel tanks , the F-15 had a range of three thousand miles , making it possible to fly from the continental United States to Europe without stopping or midair refueling . This would make it possible to quickly reinforce NATO air defenses in case of a crisis in Europe , and later would permit the Air Force to quickly dispatch F-15s to Saudi Arabia during Operation Desert Storm . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The first F-15 prototypes flew in 1972 , and serial production began in 1973 . The plane rapidly began to populate both the USAF and friendly air forces , including Israel , Japan and Saudi Arabia . The F-15 's &lt;a href= " https : //books.google.com/books ? id=KoPoB ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener noreferrer " &gt;first air-to-air kill&lt;/a&gt; was on June 27 1979 , when Israeli Air Force ace Moshe Melnik shot down a Syrian Air Force MiG-21 in his F-15A . Melnik would eventually down four aircraft from F-15As and F-15Cs , for a career total of eleven enemy fighters shot down . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Melnik 's kill was the start of a remarkable string of 104 consecutive air-to-air victories for the F-15 , with not a single Eagle lost . Israeli , Saudi and American F-15s were responsible for this impressive streak . Israeli kills included were recorded between 1979 and 1982 and included Syrian MiG-25 Foxbat interceptors , MiG-21 and MiG-23 fighters , and a number of ground attack and strike aircraft . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;During the 1991 Gulf War , the American and Saudi tally included Iraqi MiG-29 Fulcrum fighters , Mirage F-1 fighters and even an Il-76 " Candid " medium transport . One F-15E Strike Eagle even scored an air-to-air kill against an Iraqi Mi-24 attack helicopter with a laser-guided bomb . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The F-15A was eventually replaced in production by the F-15C , which included a newer AN/APG-70 synthetic aperture radar and newer F100-PW-220 engines . The latest program , nicknamed Golden Eagle , stress tested F-15Cs for wear and tear , and 178 of the planes in the best physical condition received new APG-63V3 active electronically scanned array radars and the Joint Helmet Mounted Cuing System , allowing rapid target acquisition . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;In the late 1980s , the F-15E was developed to supplement -- and eventually replace the F-111 fighter bomber as a penetrating , high speed tactical strike aircraft designed to strike deep behind enemy lines in a NATO/Warsaw Pact war in Europe . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The E model added conformal fuel tanks to increase range with a heavy bomb payload , the APG-63 radar , and a LANTRIN forward-looking infrared and laser targeting pod . With the retirement of the F-111 , the F-15E " Strike Eagle " is now the USAF 's main tactical fighter bomber . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Meanwhile , in February of this year , the USAF announced it will finally go ahead and buy brand-new F-15s even as it purchases large numbers of the F-35 Joint Strike Fighter . Updated with the latest technology , the F-15X can carry nearly two dozen air-to-air missiles and will likely work together with stealth jets to take on fleets of enemy fighters , Popular Mechanics reported . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p class= " body-text " &gt;Media reports revealed that the USAF will request eight Advanced Eagle F-15X fighters in its budget , with plans to buy 80 fighters over five years , and possibly more after that . Enough to fit out a wing of 72 aircraft , divided into three squadrons of 24 planes each , with eight spares . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The F-15X will also include large flat-panel displays for displaying aircraft information , conformal fuel tanks to give it a longer range , a digital fly-by-wire control system , a new APG-82 radar , and the Eagle Passive Active Warning Survivability System ( EPAWSS ) for protection from air-to-air missiles . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Congress has yet to pass a defense appropriations bill for fiscal year 2020 , and the Pentagon and other federal agencies have been operating under a continuing resolution since Oct. 1 . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Why does the Air Force want to buy a better version of an older non-stealth fighter when it&amp;#8217 ; s already got plenty of F-35s on the way ? The running theory is that the F-15X will complement the F-22 Raptor and the F-35 Joint Strike Fighter in the air combat mission . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Today , the USAF still employs around 177 upgraded F-15C and two-seater D models , and approximately 224 F-15E Strike Eagles . F-15s are deployed in forward bases in both Europe and Asia , most notably at RAF Lakenheath in the UK and Kadena Air Force base on the Japanese island of Okinawa. &lt;/p&gt; Carriers have a choice of a high-density , single-class economy nightmare with 146 cramped seats or a two-class configuration &gt;https : **33;12803;TOOLONG ... today&amp;#8217 ; s commercial airline industry , air carriers have a choice . Yes , they do . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Do they squish in every seat they can , and torture their prospective clients &amp;#8230 ; or , do they cut them a break , give up a few dollars , and treat them like human beings ? &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Such is life , in 2019. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Case in point -- Embraer 's new E195-E2 jet promises passengers a ride that could be either heaven or hell . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;It could be more comfortable in the airliner 's award-winning economy cabin than in other single-aisle or even some widebody jets . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Or it could be a high density , single-class nightmare with 146 seats and a knee-crushing 28-inch seat pitch . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;That choice is entirely up to the airlines , but Embraer 's thoughtful design has at least given them a good platform on which to base a superior service , Airline Ratings online reported . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The Brazilian company , which is about to become part of US aerospace giant Boeing , has put a lot of effort into designing its latest aircraft and is currently showcasing the changes on a global tour . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Powered by the Pratt &amp;amp ; Whitney PW1900G geared turbofan , the E195-E2 is the biggest of a family of three E2 jets and is due to enter service with Brazil 's Azul by the end of this year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Another member of the family , the E190-E2 , entered service in April 2018 with Norwegian carrier Wideroe and the smaller E175-E2 is due to enter service in 2021. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The three jets have maximum seating capacities ranging from 90 to 146 seats in the 28-inch high-density , single-class layout . The E195-E2 's maximum capacity adds another 22 seats to the 124 seats the E195 could carry , the report said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;But the E195-E2 can also carry 132 passengers in an all-economy layout with a more acceptable 31-inch pitch and 120 in a two-class configuration with 12 business seats and 108 31-inch pitch economy seats . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Embraer has been making commercial aircraft since the EMB110 Bandeirante in 1968 and its first generation of E-Jets entered service in 2004. &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The E2s are a significant redesign of those original planes and include upgraded avionics , a new wing , new landing gear , a new horizontal stabilizer and an updated fuselage that is more aerodynamically efficient . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The wings are designed specifically for each jet and have the highest aspect ratio of a single-aisle jet to optimize fuel burn and performance , the report said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;The fourth-generation fly-by-wire system allows for structural weight reduction while giving performance and safety margin improvements . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;figure id= " attachment406378 " style= " width : 676px " class= " wp-caption aligncenter " &gt;&lt;img class= " wp-image-406378 size-full " src= " https : **34;12838;TOOLONG ... alt= " " width= " 676 " height= " 314 " /&gt;&lt;figcaption class= " wp-caption-text " &gt;the Embraer E195-E2 can also carry 132 passengers in an all-economy layout with a more acceptable 31-inch pitch and 120 in a two-class configuration with 12 business seats and 108 31-inch pitch economy seats . It is likely to finalize initial bidding documents for the carrier by next month . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;According to the current timeline , New Delhi is likely to issue the expression of interest documents after the holiday season to ensure greater participation by foreign buyers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;A successful sale of Air India is crucial for the current government to help bridge a widening fiscal deficit exacerbated by dismal tax collections and a $20 billion corporate tax cut . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Air India has n't made any profit since its 2007 merger with state-owned domestic operator Indian Airlines Ltd . The carrier is saddled with US$ 11 billion in debt . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Last month India&amp;#8217 ; s civil aviation minister , Hardeep Singh Puri , told the Parliament that the bleeding carrier will have to be shut down if it fails to find a buyer . Pumping more taxpayer funds into the airline in a competitive market " would not be the best use of scarce financial resources of the government , &amp;#8221 ; Puri said . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;A group of ministers overseeing the sale of Air India has already approved selling the entire government stake in the carrier as well as its low-cost , overseas unit , Puri told the parliament . Modi 's administration is considering a plan to exclude $7 billion of the airline 's debt in a bid to lure buyers . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;But selling the carrier remains a challenge due to a tight civil aviation market . Airlines in India do not have the wherewithal to buy Air India . A foreign buyer can only take 49% stake under Indian laws and this may not be an attractive proposition to them . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;However , Air India has some unique strengths to offer to a potential acquirer : its prized international slots and a strong presence in the Indian market ( though diminished over the years ) . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Industry analysts warn that shutting down the airline , as the minister had threatened , is hardly an option . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;It would remove a significant number of aircraft from the market . This would cause another round of the sort of turmoil that happened soon after the grounding of Jet Airways earlier this year . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Employees , creditors and a string of other stakeholders would be left in the lurch , at the mercy of the long-drawn-out bankruptcy process . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Bankruptcy would also lead to a monopoly-like situation with IndiGo , which already has a market share now close to 50% , further tightening its grip over India 's domestic civil aviation market . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;In 2018 the Government tried to divest Air India , but there were no bidders . The government at that time offered to sell a 76% stake in Air India and retain 24% . This failed to inspire confidence amongst bidders as they felt government control of a quarter of the total stakes would lead to political interference . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;There was also lack of transparency regarding the employee-retention clause . Bidders weren&amp;#8217 ; t ready to deal with staff that couldn&amp;#8217 ; t be laid off . The height of the Cold War was nearing , and Americans were wary of what the Soviet Union was about to do next . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;Kennedy was advising families to build nuclear fallout shelters in case of an atomic event . That possibility became all too real in October , when news spread that the Soviets were planning to test the world 's largest nuclear weapon over the Arctic . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; " I was glad to get your letter about trying to stop the Russians from bombing the North Pole , " wrote JFK , " and risking the life of Santa Claus . &amp;#8221 ; &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt; " I share your concern about the atmospheric testing of the Soviet Union , not only for the North Pole but for countries throughout the world ; not only for Santa Claus but for people throughout the world . Kennedy . Credit : JFK Museum . **34;17940;TOOLONG &lt;p&gt;But President Kennedy did a lot more for that little girl than reassure her . On August 5 , 1963 , Kennedy heroically defied the military might of the Joint Chiefs , and &lt;a href= " https : **33;17976;TOOLONG ... target= " blank " rel= " noopener " &gt;signed the Limited Nuclear Test Ban Treaty&lt;/a&gt; , which banned the use of nuclear testing in the atmosphere , underwater , and in outer space . &lt;/p&gt; &lt;p&gt;With apologies to a certain young girl named Virginia , Kennedy had basically said , " Yes , Michelle , there is a Santa Claus and there will always be one for you and all children of the world .
